title: VPC ramp prober and cold-start priming validation for API/model readiness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a lightweight, automated post-deploy prober that ramps synthetic traffic against a newly provisioned VPC/private deployment to validate API readiness, model cold-start behavior, and KV-cache priming. This ticket builds a reusable Terraform hook + probe configuration that can be attached to private deploy pipelines to run a sequenced set of checks after infrastructure boots but before the release gate.

Why this is different: existing probes focus on API health or general model smoke loads. This work emphasizes a ramped, stateful priming sequence to exercise cold-start model load paths (disk->GPU), validate KV cache warm-up effectiveness, and detect regressions that only appear under scale-up bursts. The prober should also produce structured artifacts consumable by Console (traces, latency histograms, priming success markers) and return a deterministic pass/fail with actionable failure codes for CI gating and automated rollback policies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terraform hook that can be parameterized per-deployment (model variant, region, instance type) is available and documented.
- Prober executes an ordered sequence: API handshake -> model load check -> KV-cache priming queries -> ramped concurrency smoke -> long-sequence generation.
- Each step emits structured metrics: success boolean, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens generated, kv_cache_hit_rate approximation, model_load_time_ms.
- Runbook defines threshold values and rollback triggers; CI can call prober and gate release on failure.
- Artifact uploads (console traces + raw logs + checksum of loaded model) are stored to the specified S3/GS path.
- E2E test executed in staging and demonstrated to catch an introduced regression (simulated kernel timeout).
test_plan:
1) Handshake probe: single HTTP /health + small inference (< 8 tokens) to validate TLS, auth, and basic request path.
2) Model load check: trigger a larger generation (256 tokens) to force model weights to be loaded; record model_load_time_ms and success.
3) KV-cache priming: replay 50 representative prompts to populate caches and record cache hit ratio on subsequent repeated queries.
4) Ramped concurrency smoke: 1 -> 4 -> 8 short requests over 90s to observe latency slope and tail behavior.
5) Long-run stability: 5-minute low-rate stream to validate no memory leaks or increasing latencies.
6) Failure injection (optional stage): deploy a synthetic GPU timeout and verify prober returns the correct failure code and triggers rollback.
7) Verify artifacts: checksum of model binary matches expected hash and runbook markers are uploaded.

All experiments emit metrics to the Console metrics endpoint and upload logs to artifacts bucket. Test harness should be runnable as a one-shot step in Terraform/CI or as a manual job in Console.
steps:
- Design Terraform module interface to register a post-deploy 'ramp_prober' hook (inputs: deploy_id, model_name, model_version, priming_prompts_path, artifacts_bucket, prober_config_url).
- Implement prober binary (Go) that runs the ordered checks and streams structured JSON events.
- Add CloudRun/K8s job templates for running the prober inside customer VPC (private deployment) with minimal network requirements.
- Wire artifact upload and Console ingestion points.
- Add CI job to run against staging private cluster and fail build on prober failure.
- Document usage in Confluence and add pre-built priming prompt sets for common models.
- Add alerting rules in Console for prober failure metrics (immediate P1).
